chapter: Quality Serenaders, Cotton Club and union recollections
title: Who did and did not play with his bands
summary: Howard says Marshall Royal, Jack McVea, Happy Johnson and Luke Jones did not play with his bands.

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel
story.community_name: Who played in the band: reciting personnel

blocks.x: Uh-huh. And then later became trumpet and saxophone player. What about Marshall Royal at that period? Did he play with any of your bands, or was he a little too young?
No, he didn't play with any of the bands. He didn't play with any of my bands.
Uh-huh.
I'm just trying to think. I can't seem to get it in my mind if Marshall didn't play somewhere with the band, but I can't just get it in my mind.
What about Jack McVeigh, would he have played around with any of the bands, or --
Jack didn't play with us. He played by himself. You know, he played with -- I don't know what you might call it. He played by himself.
What about Happy Johnson, the trombone player.
Happy.
Happy.
No, he didn't play with me.
Andy Anderson.
Wait a minute. Andy Anderson.
Uh-huh.
Yeah, when we went to -- you know one thing? Let me go back here a little bit, Buddy.
Okay.
When we went to play at the -- the -- I'm trying to think what band we were playing with. When we went to play with the -- the what's its name band (Inaudible).
Got what?

Loyal Meyer?
No. That wasn't it either. Just had some kind of band that they were playing with and then they came and played with us.

Oh, Happy Johnson didn't play there. He sometimes with the trombone played with us, (Inaudible) -- you know.
Right.
Just getting -- what do you call that when you go out?
Like a jam, a jam session?
Yeah, jam sessions.
Uh-huh.
Happy fell in with us. Happy was good, a good trombone.
Huh?

Yes, right.

No, Luke never played with us. Luke never played with us at all. I don't know what was wrong. They told me that he was a good player, but I never heard him.
